title: Understanding the Weight Vector
text: The weight vector \(\hat{\theta}\) gives us the coefficients for each feature in the design matrix. Each coefficient tells us how much the dependent variable (in this case, mission duration in sols) changes with a one-unit change in the corresponding feature, holding all other features constant.

title: Focus on the Astronauts
text: Look at the coefficient associated with the number of astronauts in the weight vector \([-3,0.25,2]**T\). This coefficient tells you how many additional sols the mission can last for each additional astronaut.

title: Identify the Coefficient
text: Which value in the weight vector \([-3,0.25,2]**T\) corresponds to the number of astronauts?

title: Interpreting the Coefficient
text: The coefficient for the number of astronauts is $$2$$. This means that for each additional astronaut, the mission duration increases by $$2$$ sols, assuming all other factors remain constant.
